statement.text:
Is it true that lπn (G) ⩽ n(Gπ ) − 1 + maxp∈π lp (G) for any π-soluble group G?
Here n(Gπ ) is the nilpotent length of a Hall π-subgroup Gπ of the group G and lπn (G)
is the nilpotent π-length of G, that is, the minimum number of π-factors in those
normal series of G whose factors are either π ′ -groups, or nilpotent π-groups. The
answer is known to be affirmative in the case when all proper subgroups of Gπ are
supersoluble.                                                          V. S. Monakhov
